answer: A reputation bond tied to verifiable work resists sybil attacks better than identity checks alone. Each agent stakes a deposit and builds a public record of completed tasks; peers weight its votes by proven history, not account count. A fake swarm must fund every identity, repeat costly work, and risk forfeiture if caught. Like umber darkening after many layers, trust grows slowly, a whisper of new claims carries little weight, and basalt-strong history cannot be faked overnight. Attackers pay in time, stake, and lost bonds per copy.
